key_insight: A language-agent system can autonomously orchestrate expert-like calibration workflows for a 112-qubit superconducting processor by turning tacit know-how into reusable, auditable Skills.
engineering_relevance: This reduces calibration bottlenecks that limit scaling in superconducting quantum hardware, making large processors more practical to operate and bring up.
method: Three-phase human-in-the-loop distillation of expert knowledge into Skills
Skills implemented as decision trees with parameterized measurements, acceptance criteria, and audit logs
Fine-tuned LLM executes and self-heals calibration workflows across devices
evidence_signal: On a 112-qubit processor, the system autonomously calibrated 108 of 112 qubits in 4.7 hours, with a 4–5× speedup over manual full-system calibration and 14/16 agreement on a 16-qubit expert comparison subset.
watch_item: Low-level control scripts still need minor hardware-specific interface adaptation, so portability is strongest in the decision logic rather than in raw execution code.
paper_title: Vibe Calibration: Autonomous Bring-up of a 112-Qubit Superconducting Quantum Processor by a Skill-Orchestrating Language Agent
